title: Cylindrical object
spec: Create a new coordinate system with the Euler angles set to zero degrees and the translation vector set to [0.0074, 0.0074, 0.6]. Next, initiate a new face and within this face, draw a single loop. Inside this loop, draw a circle with its center at [0.0626, 0.0626] and a radius of 0.0626. Apply a scaling factor of 0.1252 to the entire sketch to adjust the dimensions accordingly. Rotate the scaled sketch using the Euler angles [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] degrees and translate it using the translation vector [0.0074, 0.0074, 0.6]. Extrude the sketch along the normal direction by 0.1 units, ensuring that the extrusion does not occur in the opposite direction. This extrusion should create a new solid body. The final dimensions of the cylindrical object will be a length of 0.1252056, a width of 0.1252056, and a height of 0.1 units.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Define the initial coordinate system transformation
translation_vector = (0.0074, 0.0074, 0.6)
euler_angles = (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)

# Create the sketch for the base of the cylinder
sketch = cq.Workplane("XY").center(0.0626, 0.0626).circle(0.0626)

# Extrude the sketch to create the cylinder
cylinder = sketch.extrude(0.1)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
cylinder = cylinder.translate(translation_vector).rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), euler_angles[0]) \
                         .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 1, 0), euler_angles[1]) \
                         .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), euler_angles[2])

# Assign the final model to 'r'
r = cylinder

# Display the final model

import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the center and radius of the circle
center = (0.0626, 0.0626)
radius = 0.0626

# Create a circle in the sketch
r = r.center(*center).circle(radius)

# Extrude the circle to create a cylinder
r = r.extrude(0.1)

# Translate the cylinder to the specified position
r = r.translate((0.0626, 0.0626, 0.0))
